# T3 Code patch ledger

Every vendored file Rennet has changed from the pristine snapshot on the `t3-vendor` branch, with why. `pnpm t3:check-ledger` fails on any vendored file that differs from the snapshot and is not listed here. Paths are relative to `vendor/t3code/`. Rennet-owned files inside the tree (`UPSTREAM.json`, this file, `digests/`, any `project.json`, any `tsconfig.rennet.json`) never need a row.

Prefer extension over edit: put Rennet code outside `vendor/` and import their modules. When upstream merges a change listed here, the fold that brings it in removes the row.

| File | Reason | Upstreamable | Upstream PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts` | Checkpoints carry optional `startCommandId` for exact round-attempt recovery. `thread.turn.start` (both command shapes) and the `thread.turn-start-requested` payload carry an optional `outputSchema`, so a turn can declare a structured-output contract. Rennet's board seats need one JSON board per turn. The same three shapes also carry an optional `mcpServers` (`name → { url, bearerTokenEnvVar? }`), so a caller can hand a turn its own MCP servers. The field names the environment variable holding the credential and never the credential: this command is persisted to the event store and replayed from it, and the Claude SDK puts its whole MCP option on the child's argument list. Server names are constrained to a TOML bare key because Codex writes them into a dotted config path, where a dot silently makes a nested table. `thread.create` (both command shapes) and the `thread.created` payload carry an optional `instructions` (a system-prompt append) and the same optional `mcpServers`, and the `OrchestrationThread` projection carries both: every turn on a Rennet session thread — including the ones the user starts from the composer, which Rennet does not author — has to run under the review's briefing and with Rennet's tools, and a provider session is built on the thread's FIRST turn, so this is a thread fact and not a turn one. The `TurnMcpServer*` schemas moved above `OrchestrationThread` because a `Schema.Struct` evaluates its field schemas at module load and the thread projection now references them. The guarantee is the dedicated credential field only — `url` is any trimmed string, so a token in a query parameter still reaches the store and the argument list. The file also defines `TurnMcpServer`/`TurnMcpServers`, the name the server owns (`SIDECAR_OWNED_MCP_SERVER_NAME`), and the helpers every hop shares (`normalizeTurnMcpServers`, `differingTurnMcpServerNames`, `collidingTurnMcpServerNames`). | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/provider.ts` | `ProviderSessionStartInput` and `ProviderSendTurnInput` carry `outputSchema` and `mcpServers`. `ProviderService` re-decodes both and strips unknown keys, so a field has to exist on the schema to survive the hop. Both also carry the THREAD's `instructions`: a provider fixes its system prompt when the session process is created, so the briefing is a session-level fact, and it travels on the turn as well so a session recovered for that turn starts briefed rather than bare. | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts` | Optional `TurnCompletedPayload.usageEpoch` identifies the Claude runtime counter (#775). `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` also carries Codex cumulative counters and provider thread identity separately from context usage (#776). `TurnCompletedPayload` carries `structuredOutput` and `durationMs`, the two facts the SDK result frame already reports and T3 dropped. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts` | Copies the command's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` onto the `thread.turn-start-requested` event it emits. Copies `thread.create`'s `instructions` and `mcpServers` onto the `thread.created` event, so the thread record carries the briefing for its whole life. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts` | Persists the accepted start command to exact provider turn association, hidden from the chat timeline. Threads `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` from the turn-start event into both `ProviderSessionStartInput` (the session starts on the first turn) and `ProviderSendTurnInput`. Reads the THREAD's `instructions` and `mcpServers` off the read model and puts them on `ProviderSessionStartInput`, and on every `ProviderSendTurnInput` so a recovery has them. At session start the MCP set is the UNION of the thread's and the turn's, computed once in `unionThreadAndTurnMcpServers`, because the adapter fixes that union when the session process is created and compares every later turn against it. `buildSendTurnRequestForThread`'s `mcpServers`, once the session is live, is NOT unconditionally that same union: it is only computed (as thread ∪ turn, same rule) when the turn itself asks for a set. A turn asking for nothing passes `mcpServers: undefined` through unchanged, so the adapter's own "a turn that asks for nothing rides whatever the session holds" rule applies — materialising the thread's set as an explicit ask instead made a LATER composer turn (no servers of its own) compare against a live session a prior turn had already grown with its own server, and `differingTurnMcpServerNames` rejected the missing server as a mismatch. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts` | Stamps settlements with a usage epoch combining query identity and SDK session identity, covering recovered queries and in-query `/clear` resets (#775). Sets the SDK's `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }` from the session's `outputSchema`, remembers the contract on the session context, fails a later turn whose schema the live session cannot serve (the SDK fixes `outputFormat` at `query()` construction and offers no setter) and says which of the two ways it failed, and puts `structured_output`/`duration_ms` from the result frame on `turn.completed`. Merges the turn's caller-supplied `mcpServers` into the SDK's and refuses a caller server under a name T3's own server holds, rather than dropping it — dropping left the session storing one set and comparing another, so the turn that opened the session was rejected as a mismatch against itself. EVERY credential is a `${VAR}` reference, T3's own included: its bearer goes into the child environment as `T3_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN`, because the SDK serialises this whole option into one `--mcp-config <json>` argument. Remembers the set on the session context and refuses a later turn asking for a different set by the names it disagrees on — the SDK fixes `mcpServers` at `query()` construction exactly as it fixes `outputFormat`, and `strictMcpConfig` is deliberately not set. Also spawns the Claude child through the SDK's `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` hook so its stdin has an `error` listener: the SDK's own transport writes the prompt without one, and a `claude` that dies before that write raised an unhandled `write EPIPE` that killed the whole server process. Binds SDK control requests to the owning child exit/error or explicit query close, so dead transports cannot leave them pending. Appends the THREAD's `instructions` to the SDK's preset system prompt (`systemPrompt.append`) so every turn on a briefed thread runs under it; nothing else in the option set changes, so the user's own settings, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md still inherit. The turn-versus-session MCP comparison needs no change: the reactor sends the union of the thread's servers and the turn's on both the start and the turn, so the set the session stores is the set a later turn is compared against. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts` | `sendTurn` carries the turn's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` into the session `resolveRoutableSession`/`recoverSessionForThread` recovers from a persisted resume cursor. Claude's SDK fixes `outputFormat` when the query is built, so a session recovered without it could never serve the turn that asked for the recovery: the adapter refused the turn as a schema mismatch, against a contract identical to the thread's own. The same recovery path carries the thread's `instructions`: a session recovered without it runs every turn after a daemon restart unbriefed, silently. `startSession` also persists the thread's `instructions`/`mcpServers` into the session's `runtimePayload` (alongside `cwd`/`modelSelection`, read back by new `readPersistedInstructions`/`readPersistedMcpServers`), and `recoverSessionForThread` — the ONE function every recovery path shares — reads them from there rather than trusting its own `input` to carry them: `interruptTurn`, `respondToRequest`, `respondToUserInput`, `rollbackConversation`, and `uploadFeedback` all recover through `resolveRoutableSession` without ever knowing the thread's briefing, so a recovery reached from any of them used to start the resumed session on `instructions: undefined`. A turn-specific `mcpServers` on the recovery input still merges on top of the persisted thread set. That same `upsertSessionBinding` call now also passes the recovery's own `effectiveInstructions`/`effectiveMcpServers` as `extra`, not just `resumed`: the directory's `upsert` shallow-merges the new runtime payload onto the old one, so a call that omitted them didn't erase the persisted briefing outright, it left a STALE one in place — a first recovery that folded in a turn-specific server (via `sendTurn`) got that union right in the session it started, but persisted the thread's bare set underneath it, and a second recovery reached through a path carrying neither (`uploadFeedback`, `interruptTurn`, etc.) read that stale set back and silently lost the server the first recovery had added. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.test.ts` | Covers the recovery above: a stale `claudeAgent` session recovered for a turn starts on that turn's output schema, and on that turn's MCP servers. The MCP case is the only test that crosses `ProviderSendTurnInput`, which is re-decoded here and strips any key it does not declare. Also covers the thread's briefing: a stale `claudeAgent` session recovered for a briefed thread starts on the briefing and the thread's servers. Also covers a briefed thread recovered by a NON-turn path: a stopped Codex session's `uploadFeedback` recovery — which never carries the thread's `instructions`/`mcpServers` on its own input — still starts the resumed session on the thread's persisted briefing and servers, and a later bare turn still reaches the adapter without the session ever restarting bare. Also covers a SECOND recovery: a `sendTurn` recovery that folds a turn-specific server onto the thread's own must persist that union, not just the thread's bare set, so a later `uploadFeedback` recovery (which carries neither) starts on both servers rather than silently losing the one the first recovery added. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts` | Preserves Codex cumulative usage breakdowns with the notification's exact turn id, including reported zero (#776). Forwards a turn's `outputSchema` to the Codex session runtime, and lowers caller-supplied `mcpServers` to `-c mcp_servers.<name>.url=…` plus `-c mcp_servers.<name>.bearer_token_env_var="…"`, naming the variable the daemon set and never carrying a credential. The credential key is written only when the caller declared one: an empty override makes Codex expect a bearer it cannot resolve, which against a real MCP server is zero requests where omitting it handshakes. Codex deep-merges every `-c` into the user's own config at every depth with no way to remove a key, so a same-named server would trade credentials and headers; the adapter therefore reads the user's configured server names (`codexConfiguredMcpServerNames`) and REFUSES a colliding caller name, the sidecar's own name included, rather than trying to out-merge it. Nothing is filtered out of the caller's set, so the session stores and compares the same thing. The adapter also states `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` rather than letting a name imply it. Codex reads its MCP configuration when the app-server is spawned, so a later turn asking for a different set is refused the way Claude's is. Carries the THREAD's `instructions` into the session runtime as `threadInstructions`: Codex has no system-prompt append, so the Claude leg's `systemPrompt.append` lands in the developer instructions instead, or a thread is briefed on one provider and bare on the other. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/CodexDeveloperInstructions.ts` | Appends the thread's own instructions after every block T3 assembles. Codex has no system-prompt append; developer instructions are its equivalent, and a thread briefed on Claude and bare on Codex would make the surface lie by provider. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts` | `buildTurnStartParams` passes `outputSchema` through to `V2TurnStartParams.outputSchema`, which the generated protocol already carries and T3 was dropping. Splits the MCP question in two: `hasConfiguredMcpServer` still answers the tool-catalog reload for any inline server, while `browserToolsAvailable` reads the new `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` option, which the adapter states. A name cannot answer it — a caller supplying a server called `t3-code` would satisfy any name test — and describing browser tools the session does not have is a lie in the Codex prompt. Holds the session's `threadInstructions` and passes them to every turn's collaboration mode, because Codex reads developer instructions per turn where Claude fixes its system prompt once at query construction. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts` | Preserves Claude usage epochs and cumulative `modelUsage` on durable settlements (#775). Persists a Codex counter baseline at turn start and carries it plus the final counter into settlement, surviving the bounded activity window and restart (#776). Projects a `turn.settled` activity from `turn.completed`, carrying the settled turn's structured output, duration, usage and cost. Nothing else in the projection carried a turn's own result, so a reader over `orchestration.subscribeThread` could not see it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.test.ts` | Covers the new adapter behaviours above: the schema becomes the SDK's `outputFormat`, no schema means no output format, a turn asking for a different contract than its session is refused, a turn arriving on a session that holds no contract is refused as that rather than as a mismatch, and the spawn hook terminates a child whose stdin breaks instead of letting the EPIPE escape. Also covers the caller-supplied MCP servers: both credentials travel as `${VAR}` references, a caller name colliding with T3's own is refused, the turn that opened the session is accepted rather than rejected against itself, no servers means no `mcpServers` option at all, and a turn asking for a different set — including one differing only in its credential variable — is refused with the differing names and the wording that says settings differ. Also covers the thread's briefing: the preset system prompt carries `append` from the thread's instructions, and carries nothing but the preset without them. | yes | pending |

| `apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts` | Adds the two `projection_threads` columns after the migrator instead of as a migration, because the migrator runs only ids GREATER than the highest id recorded and silently skips the rest: a fork that takes id 45 makes upstream's own 45 unrunnable on every database that ran ours, and a fork that takes 900 makes every future upstream migration unrunnable. Neither fails loudly. The statements are `PRAGMA`-guarded and idempotent, so upstream's id space stays untouched and a fold never has to renumber anything. The PRAGMA check and the two ALTERs now run inside one write transaction opened with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (via a local `SqlClient.makeWithTransaction`, reusing the client's own `transactionService`/`reserve`) instead of as three independent statements: `runMigrations` runs on every server start, the CLI and the server start it from separate processes against the same WAL database, and a plain `BEGIN` (or no transaction) only takes SQLite's write lock lazily on the first write, so two connections could both read the PRAGMA before either wrote, and the second one's `ADD COLUMN` failed with `duplicate column name` — aborting that connection's startup rather than hitting the idempotent-guard case this function otherwise handles. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock up front, so a second connection's own `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` blocks on the server's own `busy_timeout` until the first commits, then re-reads the columns fresh and finds them already there. | no | n/a |

Also covers the regression above directly: a first turn's own server joins the thread's at session start, and a LATER bare turn on the same thread still reaches the adapter with `mcpServers: undefined` rather than the thread-only set, so the live session (already grown by the first turn) is not restarted or refused. | yes | pending |

The shell queries do not: `OrchestrationThreadShell` carries neither. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.test.ts` | New file. Covers the two-connection race the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` fix above closes: a real child process (a separate `node:sqlite` connection, mirroring `Layers/Sqlite.test.ts`'s established pattern) takes the write lock first, adds the fork columns itself, and holds the lock while doing so; a brand-new connection through the real `makeSqlitePersistenceLive` entry point then reaches the same code path and must wait for the lock and re-read the columns as already present rather than fail with a duplicate column. Also covers the ordinary case: a freshly migrated database gets both columns, and opening the same database a second time stays idempotent (no duplicate column, no second row). | no | n/a |
